then.text: Your first Orb. Many a weaver has framed the first one. I'd frame yours. Any length that comes in carrying the right feel gets the same stamp, whoever wove it.

A length of tweed for stamping? Let me see. Handwoven, from pure wool dyed and spun on the islands, no machine anywhere in it. I can feel the beat in the weave. Seonag's work, with a bit of yours. Good.
Right. The Orb. A bang, a stamp, and that's another one for the Western Isles. Harris Tweed was woven in this length, and now it's official.
Here's a cap in the same cloth. It's warm, it's waterproof, and it's the nearest thing to armour a person can wear without a licence.

else.text: I stamp the Orb on every length. Before I do, I check the weave, the feel, and whether it smells of damp hill, which is a good sign. If you've a length that Seonag wove, bring it here.
The old test of good tweed: you could stand in a downpour in it and keep your thinking dry.
